business_scope.primary_industry_name: Video Game Kernel-Level Anti-Cheat and Integrity Middleware

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate registry distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil law. Unitary jurisdiction. Primary commercial statute is the Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), with binding constitutional jurisprudence from the Corte Constitucional.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA) with investment chapter, in force 2012
Colombia–United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty, in force 2014
Colombia–Canada Free Trade Agreement with investment protections, in force 2011
Colombia–Spain Reciprocal Investment Protection Agreement, in force 1995
Colombia–South Korea Free Trade Agreement, in force 2016
Colombia–Mexico, Colombia–Chile and Pacific Alliance framework instruments
Colombia–Netherlands, Colombia–Switzerland, Colombia–Canada and Colombia–Japan double taxation avoidance conventions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (creates UIAF); Articles 323-325 of Ley 599 de 2000 (Código Penal) as amended by Ley 1121 de 2006; Ley 2010 de 2019 introducing Article 631-4 of the Estatuto Tributario; Decreto 830 de 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUBF); DIAN Resolución 164 de 2021 (RUBF rules); UIAF and Superintendencia de Sociedades AML/CFT guidance for non-regulated service companies.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (RUBF filed with DIAN and UIAF; not publicly searchable; protected by tax reserve and habeas data legislation)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Good Standing of each non-resident corporate shareholder (or equivalent registry extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce or Companies Registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; if the country is not a Hague Apostille Convention signatory, Colombian consular legalization is required.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney granting local counsel or the designated legal representative full authority to perform name clearance, incorporation formalities and UBO filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the foreign shareholder's country of origin or the corporate shareholder's legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague jurisdictions, Colombian consular legalization of the notarized document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate resolution of the foreign shareholder approving the incorporation of the Colombian S.A.S., capital allocation, and appointment of initial directors/representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or corporate shareholder body of the foreign entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the origin-state competent authority or Colombian consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each ultimate beneficial owner and each proposed officer/director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport office or notary public authorized in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy in the country of origin followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Spanish translation of all foreign public documents (translator's certification)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator (traductor oficial) recognized by the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator's signature notarized and, where required by the receiving Colombian registry, apostilled/legalized in the source country.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, directors, legal representatives and material counterparties against Colombian UIAF PEP and money-laundering databases, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, World Bank sanction lists and adverse media. Enhanced due diligence is required if any person is a PEP, a resident of a high-risk jurisdiction, or if any 25%+ ownership chain is held through nominees, fiduciaries or opaque structures without satisfactory attribution to a natural person.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES - Registro Único Empresarial y Social (https://www.rues.org.co) operated jointly with the Cámara de Comercio of the intended corporate domicile; name availability is processed through the Chamber's homonymy/name-clearance service.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin script using Spanish orthographic conventions; where the trade name originates in a non-Latin script, a Spanish transliteration is mandatory. The legal-form suffix 'S.A.S.' must appear in the full name. Accent marks are permitted but are normalized for registry comparison. The name must be linguistically distinct from existing registered names and must not create confusion with trademarks or regulated entities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No general extension of the name-reservation window is available. If the Chamber issues an adverse name ruling, the applicant may file 'recurso de reposición y en subsidio apelación' before the same Cámara de Comercio within ten business days of notification. The Chamber must resolve the reconsideration; if denied, the file is forwarded to the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio or Superintendencia de Sociedades, as applicable. The applicant may simultaneously file a new name-reservation request. Judicial review is available through 'acción de nulidad y restablecimiento del derecho' before the administrative courts under Ley 1437 de 2011.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where the virtual-office provider operates a genuine, physically registered Colombian address with regular staff presence, mail reception, and service-of-process capacity. A pure PO box or non-physical address is not accepted. For an ISIC 6201 software development company, a virtual office may satisfy commercial registry requirements, but DIAN may require real economic substance such as locally traceable management, payroll, accounting records, and development infrastructure for tax treaty and transfer-pricing purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate. Quantified annualized probability of unannounced inspection by the Cámara de Comercio or DIAN: approximately 10% for a conventional physical office, 20% when relying on a virtual-office provider, and 35% if the registered address is residential or appears on a high-risk address indicator.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and homonymy certificate at the Cámara de Comercio of the intended corporate domicile
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Código de Comercio and the Chamber's annual fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Hague Apostille and/or consular legalization of up to five foreign corporate and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary and competent apostille/consular authority in the source country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Source-country statutory notarial and apostille tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation of all foreign documents (approximately 25 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 8-12 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized power of attorney and UBO declaration documentation prepared in Colombia
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in the Colombian corporate domicile

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO piercing, PEP, OFAC, UN and domestic sanctions screening of ultimate shareholders and directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance database provider and Colombian law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat per-subject database search fee plus professional time

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation of pre-incorporation legal opinion covering applicable licenses, investment regime, commercial registry, UBO filing and tax classification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: senior associate at USD 150-250/hour for 4-6 hours

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / virtual office service fee for the first quarter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 100-200 per month

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for expedited filings, additional notarial certifications or translations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: General contingency practice for optional expedite/supplement fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada regime), Articles 1, 5, 17 and 22; complemented by Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971) Articles 110 and 119, and Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) of the registered domicile, operating through the Registro Único Empresarial (RUE) online portal; the incorporation certificate is issued as the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private constitutional contract) with annexed bylaws (Estatutos), filed electronically through the RUE portal and authenticated by the registered legal representative; public deed is required only if real property is contributed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under Article 5 of Ley 1258 de 2008, there is no statutory minimum subscribed or paid-in capital. The S.A.S. may be formed with zero capital or with capital payable in installments over two (2) years. Nevertheless, the Chamber of Commerce charges a registration tariff scaled to the subscribed capital, our Dossier recommends a nominal paid-in part (e.g., 10%) to support bank onboarding and the Beneficial Owner filing before DIAN.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION I – SHARE SUBSCRIPTION. The incorporation instrument is ratified and the subscribed capital is acknowledged, with ten percent paid in and the balance payable within the legal term. RESOLUTION II – REGISTERED OFFICE. The principal seat is established at the address stated in the constitutional contract in Colombia; the legal representative is authorized to execute lease, utility, and internet service agreements. RESOLUTION III – OFFICERS. The Legal Representative and Deputy Legal Representative are appointed with powers to open bank accounts (SWIFT and Stripe channels), sign contracts, and represent the Company before DIAN and the Chamber of Commerce. RESOLUTION IV – ADMINISTRATIVE. The Legal Representative is authorized to complete registration formalities, obtain NIT/RUT, and sign accessory documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá – Registro Único Empresarial (RUE) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name-availability request (Certificado de Disponibilidad de Nombre) with three alternative corporate names reflecting the anti-cheat middleware activity. The Chamber verifies the proposed names against the national mercantile index to avoid collision with existing companies or trademarks. The issued certificate is valid for 30 days and is a prerequisite for drafting the constitutional document.
required_dossiers: Completed online name-availability form
Proposed corporate names (primary and two alternates)
Identity documents of each incorporator (national ID or passport)
Payment receipt for the nominal search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected for identity or trademark conflict, file a written redesignation request offering a second or third choice; if the certificate expires, reapply online and pay the fee again. Objections can be cured by adding a distinctive suffix or altering the acronym.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Constitutional Contract and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (only where in-kind real property contributions require public deed) otherwise the incorporators acting under Ley 1258 de 2008
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución and the Estatutos covering the corporate purpose (development and licensing of kernel-level anti-cheat middleware, ISIC 6201), registered office, capital structure with nominal shares, arbitration clause, and duration. If capital is paid in cash only, the document is signed by shareholders and authenticated before a notary for authentication of signatures; if real estate is contributed, the entire document must be executed as a public deed before a Notary of the registered domicile.
required_dossiers: Valid name-availability certificate
Draft constitutional contract containing all mandatory clauses under Article 17 of Ley 1258 de 2008
Identifications of shareholders and initial directors
Statement of subscribed and paid-in capital
Beneficial owner (final beneficiary) disclosure forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or a reviewing attorney flags missing statutory clauses, amend the draft to conform exactly with Article 17 of Ley 1258 de 2008 and resubmit for a fresh signature session; if shareholders object to the dispute-resolution forum, modify the arbitration clause by unanimous written consent before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and Issuance of the Mercantile Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá – Registro Mercantil via RUE / SIU windows
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed constitutional contract together with the standard RUE registration form. Pay the registration tariff (matrícula mercantil fee) assessed on subscribed capital and the Chamber-issued administrative fee. The Chamber examines the document, assigns the pre-NIT and issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, which legally distinguishes the S.A.S. as an entity separate from its shareholders.
required_dossiers: Signed Documento Privado de Constitución and bylaws
Name-availability certificate (not expired)
Chamber registration form (RUE/SIU)
Identity documents of the legal representative and Deputy Secretary
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a required-diligence notice (requerimiento), the incorporators must cure the stated deficiencies in writing within the granted term (typically 10 business days). If the registration tariff is underpaid, pay the difference and request recalculation; in case of parallel trademark opposition, withdraw the name and re-file under a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration – RUT, NIT, Electronic Invoicing and Export Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (RUT virtual portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the pre-NIT assigned by the Chamber, file the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) electronically, declaring ISIC 6201 as the primary economic activity, selecting the general corporate income tax regime, and updating the business address. The same procedure activates electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) and obtains the digital certificate. For software export revenue, the RUT must also include the exporter status with customs cooperation signal, enabling SWIFT and Stripe collection without import-export permits.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal issued by the Chamber
Authenticated copy of the constitutional contract
Identity document of the legal representative
RUT application form completed online (Formulario 002-0106 virtual)
Corporate email address and local contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the CIIU classification or the exporter authorization, submit a RUT correction (actualización) attaching the Chamber certificate as supporting evidence. If the portal blocks the pre-NIT, contact DIAN's contact center and request the human-assisted validation appointment; any penalties for late filing are waived where the initial rejection is procedural.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking, Occupational Safety, Beneficial Owner and Data-Protection Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banks (corporate account), ARL (Riesgos Laborales), SIC (Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio) and the local Fire Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account presenting the NIT, the Chamber certificate, board resolution, and identification of ultimate beneficial owners; the account is enrolled in SWIFT wire and Stripe payout rails. Register the company with a licensed ARL before hiring first employees and enroll workers in the PILA payroll system. Obtain the Certificado de Bomberos (fire safety) for the registered office, and register all client/employee databases with SIC under Law 1581 of 2012 through the Registro Nacional de Bases de Datos. File the Beneficiario Final (UBO) report with DIAN within 3 months of formation.
required_dossiers: NIT/RUT certificate
Chamber Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Copy of the First Board Resolution appointing officers
ARL affiliation form and PILA documentation
Fire-safety inspection request
SIC database registration form
UBO/Beneficial Owner declaration under DIAN Resolution 000016/2023
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's KYC raises objections, provide the enhanced due diligence package with extraction from the Chamber registry and the Full Board Resolution. For SIC data-registration errors, submit an electronic rectification through the SIC portal within 10 days. If the local fire inspector orders structural modifications, implement the mitigation and request a re-inspection within the 30-day corrective term.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial manufacturing license is required for ISIC 6201 software-only operations. The Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) is the residual authority for commercial regulations, trademark registration, and personal-data registry oversight.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no statutory operating permit is required for kernel-level anti-cheat middleware development. Voluntary trademark registration before SIC is recommended; if the company later self-hosts hardware servers, a municipal land-use permit and environmental compliance for electronic waste (RAEE – Resolución 1512 de 2010) will apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) with municipal environmental authorities (CAR) for office-level permitting
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – software development and digital middleware licensing are not listed in Decree 1076 de 2015 as activities requiring an EIA; only physical industrial facilities with wastewater, VOC or hazardous-waste emissions are categorized as I, II or III risk levels.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the pure software activity. The registered office must contract approved urban waste collection and treat any negligible office wastewater under municipal sewer discharge regulations; if small server racks are installed, compliance with RAEE and WEEE directives for electronic disposal and applicable electrical safety standards must be documented.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must obtain the Certificado de Bomberos (fire-safety certificate) confirming structural load, fire-exit and extinguisher compliance; additionally, under Resolución 2400 de 1979 occupational health clearance and ARL (Riesgos Laborales) enrollment are required before the first employee works on the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official portal www.dian.gov.co; transactional fiscal registration and electronic invoice portal: MUISCA (muisca.dian.gov.co)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Appoint a resident legal representative through a properly notarized and apostilled power of attorney. Step 2: File the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) electronically in MUISCA, indicating entity type S.A.S. and 'domicilio en el exterior' where applicable; DIAN assigns the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). Step 3: Activate the taxpayer attributes including 'Responsable de IVA' (Régimen Común) and, if applicable, withholding agent status. Step 4: Obtain electronic invoicing habilitación through a DIAN-authorized technology provider (Proveedor Tecnológico). Step 5: Register the bank account for export proceeds with a Colombian intermediary bank and open the foreign currency market (Mercado Cambiario) operational line.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Colombian S.A.S. is a separate and autonomous taxpayer, subject to corporate income tax, VAT, and complementary taxes; no pass-through or fiscal transparency applies; Colombian source rules apply for outward services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists. Mandatory entity-level taxation applies. Available statutory elections include: (i) Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) for entities with prior-year gross revenues up to 100,000 UVT (approximately COP 4,980 million in 2025); (ii) election of monthly VAT refund cycles for goods exporters or quarterly/annual recovery cycles; (iii) application for 'exportador de servicios' certification to streamline refund processing; (iv) tax group consolidation for qualifying business groups subject to prior DIAN authorization; and (v) request for an advance pricing/characterization agreement with DIAN for cross-border service transaction treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (IVA - Impuesto al Valor Agregado), governed by the Estatuto Tributario, Articles 420 et seq.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic turnover exemption threshold for corporate taxpayers: an S.A.S. is automatically classified in the VAT common regime and must register in the RUT before the first taxable event. The simplified-regime threshold (gross income not exceeding 3,500 UVT, approximately COP 174.3 million in 2025) is limited to natural persons trading goods and does not extend to companies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica de Venta) with DIAN pre-validation for all responsible taxpayers, including exporters. Each invoice is transmitted as XML to the MUISCA web services through an authorized Proveedor Tecnológico; DIAN performs real-time validation of the numbering range, RUT attributes, and tax items; upon acceptance the taxpayer affixes the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) as the digital stamp and a QR code. Export transactions require a special export-series electronic invoice reconciled with customs documentation. DIAN event codes (CODI, COUS, COMA) must be tracked. Failure to issue compliant electronic invoices invalidates VAT credits and expense deductibility and triggers penalties under Articles 652 through 653 of the Estatuto Tributario.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under Article 481 of the Estatuto Tributario. Services qualify as 'Servicios Exportados' at the 0% VAT rate upon cumulative compliance with: (i) the service is used exclusively abroad or in the production of goods/services abroad; (ii) the recipient is a non-resident and not domiciled in Colombia; (iii) the benefit is not exploited in Colombia; (iv) the consideration is paid in foreign currency and repatriated through the Colombian foreign exchange market; and (v) the service is not associated with goods physically located in Colombia. Kernel-level anti-cheat middleware and SaaS licenses supplied to foreign gaming operators generally satisfy these requirements; a documented ownership and revenue-mix analysis should be maintained to substantiate the export characterization.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Factura Electrónica de Exportación (export series FEV bearing the CUFE)
Export contract or service agreement with the foreign counterparty
Customs Export Declaration (DEX) and Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (required for physical media components)
Declaración de Cambio, Form 1, and Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas issued by the Colombian intermediary bank
Management letter and accounting support evidencing the VAT credit pool (IVA descontable) and refund application using Formulario 350
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may audit export zero-rating positions for up to five years and may retroactively disallow the 0% rate where substantive, documentary, or foreign-exchange repatriation conditions are unmet. Consequences include: collection of the 19% IVA plus monthly default interest; the inaccuracy penalty equal to 100% of the greater of the omitted VAT or the refund improperly obtained; revocation of the exporter status; disablement of the electronic invoicing system; and criminal prosecution under Articles 402 and 403 of the Código Penal for fraudulent tax refunds, punishable by 48 to 108 months of imprisonment and fines equal to the value obtained. Separate foreign-exchange infractions for non-repatriation are sanctioned by DIAN with fines up to 150% of the uncollected sum.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Mercantile Registration Renewal (Renovacion de la Matricula Mercantil) and filing of certified annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Camara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Camara de Comercio de Bogota)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a surcharge of 3% per month on the registration tariff; persistent non-renewal leads to administrative de-registration of merchant status, suspension of commercial registration and risk of strike-off via cancellation of the mercantile certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Shareholders' Meeting and approval of financial statements; registration of meeting minutes at the Chamber of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate organ (General Shareholders' Meeting); certified minutes filed with Camara de Comercio jointly with the March renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end (by 31 March for a calendar-year S.A.S.)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors' liability for non-convocation; loss of the benefit of limited liability against third parties for undisclosed acts; the Chamber of Commerce may reject the annual renewal until the meeting minutes are registered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income and Complementary Tax Return (Declaracion de Renta, Form 210)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Direccion de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between mid-August and early September per DIAN resolution calendar keyed to the last two digits of NIT (2025 tax cycle: 12 August - 8 September)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 1% per month or fraction of the greater of tax due or 5% of gross income, minimum 10 UVT (approx. USD 125); late payment default interest of approx. 1.5% per month; chronic non-filing permits DIAN estimated assessment and, combined with renewal failure, administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Third-Party External Information Return (Informacion Exogena, Form 2276 / Formats 1001-1017)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in early-to-mid July per NIT-based DIAN schedule (FY 2024 cycle: 7-15 July 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Article 651 Tax Code fines up to 10,000 UVT (approx. USD 108,000) for non-filing; penalty of 5% of the value of unreported transactions when quantifiable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Estados de Beneficiario Final - UBO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN UBO platform (reporting co-ordinated with UBO confirmation at the Chamber of Commerce renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 January following the reporting calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Article 651 Tax Code fines up to 10,000 UVT for non-submission or material inaccuracy; unresolved UBO information can block the March 31 mercantile renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Transfer Pricing Local File, Informative Return (Form 120) and Master File (if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same NIT-based schedule as the annual income tax return (annually August - September)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file: penalty of up to 1% of the aggregate value of controlled transactions, minimum 2,955 UVT; transfer-pricing adjustments carry a 20% surcharge on the resulting income tax underpayment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Industry and Commerce Tax (ICA) annual return to the local treasury
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal treasury (in Bogota: Secretaria Distrital de Hacienda - SHD system; rates vary by municipality)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due per municipal NIT-based calendar; Bogota annual and complementary ICA return due in mid-to-late April (2025 cycle: 21-29 April); bimestral scheme applies to higher-revenue taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 1% per month (minimum 1 SMMLV, maximum 10 SMMLV) plus default interest; persistent non-payment enables municipal enforced collection and bank attachment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) is mandatory when the S.A.S. holds prior-year gross assets or gross income exceeding 5,000 SMMLV (approx. COP 7,100 million / USD 1.8 million for 2025), when 30 or more employees are engaged, or when the founders elected such office in the bylaws; otherwise, audit is voluntary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian adoption of IFRS: NIIF Plenas (full IFRS) for Group 1 public-interest entities and NIIF para PYMES (IFRS for SMEs) for the standard mid-market S.A.S.; financial statements must be presented in COP, prepared with 31 December year-end and approved by shareholders by 31 March.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal representative must submit the DIAN Beneficiario Final annual update by 30 January for the preceding calendar year, disclosing every individual with direct or indirect ownership or control of 5% or more of equity, voting rights or de facto control. All share transfers during the year must be contemporaneously recorded in the Register of Shareholders and aligned with the Chamber of Commerce UBO confirmation filed with the March 31 renewal; changes in ownership must be updated in the DIAN UBO portal within 30 days of the transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro de Registro de Accionistas (Register of Members)
Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas (Minute Book of the Shareholders' Meeting)
Libro de Registro de Nombramientos o Actas de la Junta Directiva (Register of Directors/Minute Book, if board exists)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 1,500 per year for registered office, legal representation and Chamber of Commerce annual compliance services in Bogota or Medellin
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,200 - 9,500 per year for a mid-size S.A.S. (external audit or Revisor Fiscal engagement, depending on transaction volume and consolidation complexity)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Unqualified income taxed at 35%; qualified software/gaming anti-cheat projects may access the 200% R&D deduction under Article 158-1 E.T., accelerated depreciation for software investments, and, subject to Ministry of Culture/COLCIENCIAS certification, the "economía naranja" partial income-tax exemption for new creative/software ventures. Absent certification, no statutory tax holiday applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 - Declaración de Renta y Complementarios, filed electronically through DIAN Muisca portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Calendar fiscal year. Return due in August-September of the following year according to NIT ending digit on the annual DIAN tax calendar (e.g., FY2024 returns: 16 August through 11 September 2025).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross revenue from licensing/kernel-level anti-cheat middleware, SaaS subscriptions, and related technical services attributable to the Colombian company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident with no Colombian PE reports no revenue on Form 210; Colombian-source payments are subject to final withholding at source by the payer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct direct costs (hosting, salaries, third-party SDKs) and ordinary expenses necessary for software development and sales, supported by invoices and transfer pricing files.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only if attributable to a Colombian PE and backed by the adjusted arm's length documentation; unallocated head-office costs are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after leases, depreciation, net operating loss compensation and any qualifying exempt creative-industry income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a PE exists, compute PE profit after expense apportionment. Without a PE, omit; profits are taxed exclusively through withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result of 35% statutory CIT on taxable income, reduced by credits (withholdings, foreign tax credits, ICA tax credit) to determine final tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE filers must attach Form 210 evidence of credible local tax withholdings; non-PE foreign parent not required to enter an amount on this line.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Extemporaneous return penalty: 5% of the amount of tax due per month or fraction delayed, capped at 100%; where no tax is due, 1% of gross income per month, capped at 100%; minimum sanctions for zero returns; outstanding tax accrues daily interest. Failure to file electronically or underreporting may trigger DIAN sanctions up to 100%-200% of omitted amounts and can suspend taxpayer status.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders when sourced from profits that have already borne CIT; distributions out of non-taxed/exempt profits are treated as ordinary Colombian-source income and taxed at 35% (Art. 245/246 E.T.).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a lower DTA rate, the foreign shareholder must (i) obtain an official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the home-country tax administration, (ii) provide the Colombian paying SAS with a beneficial-ownership certificate identifying the ultimate recipient, and (iii) file the DTA relief application with DIAN (generally via Muisca) before or at the time of distribution. The payer must retain the TRC, the DTA declaration, and underlying shareholding proof (minimum shareholding/period tests) for the five-year prescription period; no advance ruling is needed unless the treaty prescribes a specific procedural form. Colombia's DTAs (e.g., Spain, Chile, Canada, South Korea, Mexico, India, U.K., Switzerland) typically reduce the dividend WHT to 0%-10% depending on shareholding threshold.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 20% WHT on cross-border royalties and 15% WHT on foreign-debt interest (from Colombian source). Treaties may reduce royalties to 5%-17.5% and interest to 0%-10%; payments to blacklisted/haven jurisdictions may lose treaty access and be subject to the statutory rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and informative TP return (Form 120/220 equivalents subject to DIAN resolution) arise when gross assets or gross income in Colombia exceed approximately COP 4,706,500,000 (100,000 UVT) AND cross-border controlled transactions exceed approximately COP 47,065,000 (1,000 UVT per related party/per transaction). Lower thresholds or zero-threshold reporting apply for transactions with non-cooperative/low-tax jurisdictions and for taxpayers with net worth/income above the ordinary threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not have a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the DIAN aggressively applies substance-over-form, business-purpose, and beneficial-ownership doctrines under GAAR Article 869 E.T. and transfer-pricing Article 260-3 E.T. For the CO_SAS gaming anti-cheat entity, economic substance is demonstrated by payroll, actual executive/engineering decisions residing in Colombia, server/development infrastructure, and real commercial risk; lack of substance is recharacterized as a sham, causing disregarded transactions and treaty denial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a false Form 210 that omits Colombian-source license/revenue streams, knowledge-based overpayment of intercompany royalties, or producing forged transfer pricing documentation to DIAN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanction under Article 434A Criminal Code (Ley 1762/2015): imprisonment 48-108 months, a fine equal to 20%-50% of the evaded tax, and exclusion from state contracting; DIAN may nullify returns and impose 100%-200% penalty on omitted amounts plus daily interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/legal representatives who sign or order false returns are jointly and severally liable under Article 794 E.T. for the corporate tax debt; they may face criminal imprisonment, personal asset embargoes, a judicial exit/travel ban, and suspension of their commercial registration, without access to corporate veil protection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a CO_SAS with no real staff, no operational office, no board decisions, and no technical substance as a mere invoicing/royalty conduit for gaming anti-cheat fees routed through Stripe or SWIFT to offshore shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN disregards the legal personality under the veil-piercing doctrine (Law 1258/2008, Art. 42; Art. 869 E.T.), determines CIT at the real beneficiary level, and applies recharacterization penalties; the registry may cancel the mercantile registration and impose fines up to 100% of transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders and managers of the artificial SAS are held civilly and criminally liable for all unpaid corporate taxes; foreign directors risk personal seizure, a foreign-exchange and travel restriction order, and up to 20 years of imprisonment if the sham is used to launder proceeds through UIAF-reportable payment rails.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting funds by Stripe or SWIFT wires that derive from online fraud, illegal gaming exploitation, ransomware, or sanctioned countries while deliberately avoiding AML surveillance or bank/KYC requests (structuring below reporting thresholds).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code Art. 323 (financial assistance for money laundering): imprisonment 9-15 years (extended for aggravated laundering) plus a fine of 1,300 to 50,000 statutory minimum monthly wages; UIAF and Fiscalía can seize bank, Stripe, and SWIFT records; VIOLATION OF anti-terrorism finance laws carries additional 10-20 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or compliance officers who ignore red flags or permit the payments are treated as co-authors of laundering; personal and corporate assets are confiscated, directors face immediate travel bans, disqualification from office, and up to 25 years in prison under the aggravated regime, with the corporate veil being pierced to reach shareholders.
